title: GitLab SSO with Casdoor: OpenID Connect Setup
headline: Single sign-on for self-managed GitLab
summary: Self-managed GitLab signs users in through OmniAuth providers, including any OpenID Connect provider. With Casdoor as the provider, developers use one account for GitLab and the rest of your tools.

steps.title: Add Casdoor to gitlab.rb
steps.text: GitLab only talks to OpenID providers over HTTPS, so serve Casdoor over HTTPS. Add this to `/etc/gitlab/gitlab.rb` and run `sudo gitlab-ctl reconfigure`.

steps.title: Map Casdoor groups (GitLab Premium and Ultimate)
steps.text: To make members of a Casdoor group GitLab administrators, or to mark contractors as external users, add a `gitlab` block inside `client_options`. Set the Casdoor application's **Token group format** to **Name** so the values match.

steps.title: Sign in
steps.text: The sign-in page now has a **Casdoor** button. People who already have a GitLab account can connect Casdoor under **User settings → Account → Service sign-in**.

tips: `omniauth_allow_single_sign_on` lets GitLab create an account on first sign-in, and `omniauth_block_auto_created_users = false` lets new users in without waiting for an administrator to approve them.
`uid_field: "sub"` ties each GitLab identity to the Casdoor user ID, which doesn't change when a user is renamed.

faqs.question: Do I need GitLab Premium?
faqs.answer: Not for single sign-on: any self-managed GitLab can use Casdoor as its OpenID Connect provider. Rules based on OIDC group membership (required, external and admin groups) need GitLab Premium or Ultimate.

faqs.question: I compiled GitLab from source. Where do the settings go?
faqs.answer: Put the same provider settings under `omniauth` in `config/gitlab.yml`; GitLab's OpenID Connect documentation shows that format next to the gitlab.rb one.
